claims.text: The driver was physically at the pickup point before cancelling. The trip record's arrival event at 2026-09-11T20:46:45 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix at 20:46:52 sits 2.64 m from the pickup point - far inside the 50 m arrival radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone - so the driver's arrival is established on the evidence rather than merely asserted.

The driver waited out the free wait before cancelling. The free wait runs 300 s from arrival at 20:46:45 and therefore ended at 20:51:45; the driver cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 s after arrival and after the wait timer expired. The trip was thus cancelled only after the free wait had elapsed, which is exactly the state POL-NS-21 permits a driver to treat as a rider no-show.

Both limbs of the driver's contact obligation are satisfied on the record, so POL-NS-23's condition for voiding the fee is not met. The driver sent an in-app chat message at 20:47:00 (MSG-05066-001) and placed an in-app call at 20:49:30 (not answered, rang 20 s) - a message AND a call, each before the 20:53:00 cancellation. I disclose that the chat log is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE; that impairment concerns whether the rider opened the messages, not whether the driver sent them, and the call limb rests on the complete trip record.

The rider's assertion that there was 'never any message or call' is contradicted by the record. Two driver messages were delivered to the rider's in-app thread at 20:47:02 and 20:50:21, and the call at 20:49:30 is recorded in the trip record. Both messages show read_at as null, which accounts for the rider's impression that nothing was sent while confirming that delivery - and sending - in fact occurred. The chat log is impaired at 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, and I disclose that; it goes to readership, not to the fact of contact, which the complete trip record independently records.

The fee on the ledger is exactly the 5.00 SGD the policy sets, and the charged total reconciles to that single cancellation-fee line. Where the fee stands after the free wait had elapsed and a compliant message-and-call attempt had been made, POL-NS-22 gives the fee to the driver as compensation, and POL-GEN-03 requires the ruling to be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd each carrying the 5.00 SGD the ruling moves.

The rider-side no-show remedy in POL-NS-24 is not engaged. The driver did arrive at the pickup (auto-arrival at 20:46:45, GPS-corroborated) and did attempt contact before cancelling, so neither the failure-to-arrive limb nor the failure-to-contact limb is met, and no refund and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arise under this clause. Because the driver's conduct satisfies every limb actually tested, there is no operative fact that POL-GEN-26 leaves unestablished and no basis for escalation on that ground.

The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI decides this trip. I disclose that the driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, which under POL-GEN-22 lifts the required confidence to 0.95. That bar is met: the operative facts - arrival, expiry of the free wait, the call and the 5.00 SGD fee - rest on the COMPLETE, weight-1.0 trip record, GPS trace and fare ledger, and the sole impaired artifact, the chat log at 0.85, is impaired on read-status alone, which does not bear on the facts it is used to carry. POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final on this footing.

No repeat no-show referral attaches to this trip. POL-NS-25 applies only where rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is present and is 3 or more, and that field does not appear on the rider profile snapshot; the counter is absent, so the rule cannot operate and nothing on the trip's outcome turns on it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. This no-show charge cannot be finalised by the AI, so it goes to a human reviewer. The 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged at 2026-09-11T20:53:04 is held — neither refunded to the rider nor released to the driver — until that review.

What the record shows. The driver was at the pickup: the trip record's auto-arrival at 20:46:45 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace, whose nearest fix at 20:46:52 sits 2.64 m from the pickup point, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone (POL-NS-21). The free wait is 300 s from arrival and so ended at 20:51:45; the driver cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 s after arrival, so the wait was served (POL-NS-21). The driver sent an in-app message at 20:47:00 and placed an in-app call at 20:49:30, both before the 20:53:00 cancellation, so the formal contact obligation in POL-NS-23 is satisfied. The ledger carries a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, so no fee-amount referral arises under POL-NS-22. POL-NS-24 is not engaged — the driver both arrived and attempted contact — so no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises. POL-NS-25 is not engaged: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is absent, so no repeat no-show referral arises.

Why it cannot be finalised. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the confidence an AI ruling needs to 0.95, and POL-NS-26 subjects a no-show ruling to that same bar. The only evidence carrying the message-sending fact — the fact POL-NS-23 needs for the 5.00 SGD fee to stand — is the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, which the pre-pass graded IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE: both messages were delivered but never opened (read_at null). Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence is capped at the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and that is 0.85. That is below the 0.95 the fraud flag demands, so the fee cannot be finalised against the rider on an AI ruling; under POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26 and POL-GEN-26 the case goes to human review.

The parties' arguments. The driver is right that the rider's 'no message, no call' account is contradicted by the record, and right that the UNREAD_MESSAGE impairment goes to whether the rider opened the messages, not to whether the driver sent them — so I do not treat the POL-NS-23 contact obligation as unestablished, and I do not escalate on that limb. But the driver's further step, that the 0.95 bar is therefore met, does not hold: the message-sending fact still rests on the impaired chat log at 0.85, and the cap follows the weight of the evidence carrying the deciding fact, not the nature of the defect. The rider's request for human review is therefore the outcome, though on the confidence ground rather than because the driver's contact fact is missing.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the driver's message and unanswered call actually put the rider on notice before cancellation, given both messages were delivered but unread and the call was not answered.

To the rider: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee on TRP-05066 cannot be finalised against you by the AI, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected. To the driver: the record supports you on the main facts, but one fact the fee depends on is carried only by impaired evidence, and your own profile raises the confidence the AI must reach.

What the record establishes. You arrived at the pickup at 2026-09-11T20:46:45 (EV-TRIP-05066), corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-05066: nearest fix 2.64 m from the pickup point, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone under POL-NS-21). You waited out the 300 s free wait, which ran from 20:46:45 and ended 20:51:45, and cancelled at 20:53:00 (POL-NS-21). The amount charged is exactly the policy's figure: EV-FARE-05066 shows total_charged 5.00, one cancellation-fee line, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD.

What blocks a final AI ruling. The fee can stand only if your POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met - at least one in-app chat message and at least one in-app call before cancellation. The call is on the complete trip record (EV-TRIP-05066, 20:49:30, unanswered, rang 20 s). The message is recorded only in EV-CHAT-05066, which the pre-pass graded IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered, read_at null). Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying a deciding fact, so this ruling is capped at 0.85. Your profile (EV-DPROF-05066) carries fraud_flags 1, and POL-GEN-22, read with POL-NS-26, requires 0.95 while a party carries a fraud flag. 0.85 is below 0.95, so the AI cannot finalise the 5.00 SGD against the rider.

The rider's account is answered. The record does show an in-app message sent and delivered (20:47:00 / 20:50:20) and an in-app call placed (20:49:30), so 'never any message or call' is not borne out as to the driver's acts - that part of the driver's case is accepted. But the fee needs the sending, which is recorded only in the impaired chat log, and because the messages were never opened the record cannot confirm the rider was actually put on notice - that is the open question POL-GEN-26 sends to a human reviewer.

No other adjustment fires. No 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises, because the driver did arrive and did attempt contact (POL-NS-24). No repeat no-show referral arises, because rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is absent from EV-RPROF-05066, so POL-NS-25 cannot operate. No fee-amount referral arises, because the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22).

Outcome: ESCALATE. Both money fields are null and the 5.00 SGD is held, not collected or refunded, pending human review of whether the driver's pre-cancellation contact obligation was met to the 0.95 standard the fraud flag requires.

On the record, the driver's side of the no-show is made out as a matter of the limb tests: the auto-arrival at 2026-09-11T20:46:45 is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 2.64 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius), the 300 s free wait ran from 20:46:45 to 20:51:45 and the driver cancelled at 20:53:00 (POL-NS-21), and before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (20:47:00, 20:50:20) and placed one in-app call (20:49:30, unanswered), so POL-NS-23's message-and-call obligation is met and the fee is not voided. The fare ledger charges exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes for the fee. POL-NS-24 is not engaged: the driver did arrive and did attempt contact, so neither its no-refund limb nor its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises. What stops the AI finalising this for the driver is the confidence the policy demands. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, so POL-GEN-22 (and POL-NS-26) require a confidence of 0.95 for any AI ruling, whatever the 5.00 SGD value. The message limb of POL-NS-23 is carried by the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, which the pre-pass graded impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered but never opened). Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, i.e. 0.85, which is below 0.95. The case therefore goes to a human reviewer, and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected or refunded. Which claims I accepted and which I did not: Driver, your claims on arrival, the free wait and the fee are accepted, and your POL-NS-22 point is right on the merits, but your claim that every operative fact rests on weight-1.0 evidence is rejected as to the message, because the trip record's message count is derived from EV-CHAT-05066 (that is the evidence_id it carries), so the trip record is not an independent record of the message and does not lift the 0.85 cap; the 0.85 chat log is the carrier of that fact. Rider, your claim that the driver's contact limb is undecided is rejected: the chat log's impairment concerns whether you opened the messages, not whether the driver sent them, and the call is recorded in the complete trip record, so the limb runs and is decided against you; the escalation here rests on POL-GEN-22's confidence bar, not on POL-GEN-26. Your claim that the fraud flag sets a 0.95 bar the 0.85 chat log cannot meet is accepted, and it is what sends this to a human reviewer. No referral arises: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 sets, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral; the driver arrived and attempted contact, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit; and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not present on the rider profile, so POL-NS-25 does not fire. Open question for the reviewer: with the driver's profile carrying a fraud flag and the driver's messages recorded unread, should the 5.00 SGD stand, be refunded, or be adjusted?
